# session-recorder

> Writer and reader for OKL v1, a plain-text, tab-separated log format for operant session events (responses, reinforcer start and end, state changes, phase markers) with a self-describing header and codebook.

session-recorder is part of OperantKit, a set of Python/Rust packages for designing and running operant and respondent conditioning experiments (reinforcement schedules, session recording, analysis). Use it instead of a hand-written CSV or JSON logger: the file carries the session metadata and the type of every column, reads back into typed event objects, and follows a written specification with conformance files.

## Install

```bash
pip install session-recorder
```

## Minimal example

```python
from experiment_core import ResponseEvent
from session_recorder import OklSink, read_log

sink = OklSink("demo.okl")
sink.write_header(session_name="demo", clock_type="VirtualClock", session_start=0.0, metadata={"dsl": "FR 3"})
sink.emit(ResponseEvent(id=1, timestamp=0.5))
log = read_log("demo.okl")
print(log.meta.session_name, log.events)  # demo [ResponseEvent(id=1, timestamp=0.5, operandum=None)]
```

`OklSink` implements the `experiment_core.EventSink` protocol, so it can be passed as the `sink` of a session-runner `SessionRunner`.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder/blob/main/README.md): role, 30-second example, why not to hand-roll a logger, quick start
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder/blob/main/AGENTS.md): when to use this package and what not to do
- [Format reference](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder/blob/main/docs/en/format.md): OKL v1 schema as implemented here

## Related packages

- [OperantKitLog](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog): the OKL v1 specification (grammar, header, codebook, wire format, conformance files)
- [experiment-core](https://github.com/OperantKit/experiment-core): the event types that are written and read (`pip install experiment-core`)
- [session-runner](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-runner): drives a session and forwards its events to `OklSink` (`pip install session-runner`)
- [session-analyzer](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-analyzer): cumulative records and statistics from OKL v1 logs (`pip install session-analyzer`)
